# Workflow — cycles, merges, derivation

#agent-authored
Provenance: [../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md](../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md)
Terms: [cycle](glossary.md#cycle) · [derivation job](glossary.md#derivation-job) · [checks](glossary.md#checks) · [derived view](glossary.md#derived-view) · [deps](glossary.md#deps) · [operator](glossary.md#operator)

## The unit of work is the cycle

#human-authored
The idea behind the workflow in this system is similar to that of a feature branch - the user creates a branch `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, where <name> is the expected focus of a series of exchanges. Exchanges, being single turn ephemeral communication between the operator and agent, are mapped to single commits, which aggregate progressively as a "cycle" of work. Once the cycle has been resolved, or once reaching the point that the operator wants to cease work, they issue a pull request to merge work into main from that branch. The commits made by the operator notably do not include derived views which are deterministically generated - given they are not to be changed by operators or agents, they are retained on main and can only be touched by CI/CD.

#agent-authored
A cycle is a branch: `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, named when it is opened
— intent declared before the work exists. A cycle carries any change
class — exchanges and sidecars, docs, tools, taxonomy nodes — with one
exclusion: **derived views never change on a branch**. Views belong to
`main` and are written only by the derivation job.

## During a cycle

- Each capture is committed to the branch as it is audited:
  `git add exchanges && git commit`. One commit per exchange keeps the
  branch legible; other change classes commit at whatever granularity
  reads well.
- The pre-commit hook runs the **record checks**
  (`tools/check_records.exs`: authorship, exchanges, deps) on every
  commit. `check_views` does not gate branch commits — branch views are
  expected to lag.
- `deps:` may target exchanges on `main` and exchanges earlier in the
  same branch — nothing else. A dep that wants an exchange from another
  open cycle means the two cycles are one cycle, or one merges first.
- Cycles may run in parallel. The only cross-cycle collision surface is
  two branches minting the same `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>` filename, which git
  surfaces as an ordinary conflict at the second merge.

## Closing a cycle

1. Push the branch and open a PR to `main`.
2. The PR-required CI runs the record checks; red blocks the merge.
3. **When an agent worked the cycle, the agent writes the PR
   description as the merge message it would have written** — the agent
   half of the cycle's dual entry.
4. The operator squash-merges with a **hand-written message describing
   the cycle** — the operator half, and the ratification. `main`'s
   history is one commit per cycle, each carrying the operator's own
   account; divergence between the two halves is visible on the PR
   forever.
5. Nothing merges itself: merging is the operator's act, always.

## After the merge — derivation

On every push to `main`, the derivation job regenerates all derived
views (taxonomy leaf indexes, threads), runs the full check suite
(`check_all`, including `check_views`), and — only when views changed —
commits the regeneration, touching `#derived` paths only, with its own
name on the commit. `main` therefore has exactly two writers: the
operator's merge, and this job (INV-5′). If derivation or any check
fails, the job fails loudly and commits nothing.

## `main` protections

The gate is a repository ruleset on `main` (operator-console act:
recorded here, applied there): a PR is required before merging, the
`records` check is required to pass, and deletions and force pushes
are blocked. Sole bypass actor: deploy keys — one write-enabled key
exists, held by the derivation job as the `DERIVE_SSH_KEY` secret, so
the job is `main`'s only direct pusher. The operator lands work
through PR merges like any writer; the job's workflow token is
read-only, so the deploy key is its single write path. The reasoned
walk-through — every console step and why — is in
[setup.md](setup.md).

## Failure handling

- Red record check on a branch commit: fix the record, commit again —
  the file is not yet ratified; editing it is the audit working.
- Red PR check: same, on the branch, before merge.
- Red derivation job on `main`: the merge introduced a state the checks
  reject — open a correction cycle; never push fixes directly to
  `main`.

1	# Constitution — the information model
2	
3	#agent-authored
4	Provenance: [../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md](../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md)
5	Terms: [ledger](glossary.md#ledger) · [exchange](glossary.md#exchange) · [docs](glossary.md#docs) · [tools](glossary.md#tools) · [taxonomy](glossary.md#taxonomy) · [derived view](glossary.md#derived-view) · [nursery rule](glossary.md#nursery-rule) · [authorship markers](glossary.md#authorship-markers) · [sidecar](glossary.md#sidecar) · [no silent caps](glossary.md#no-silent-caps) · [supersession](glossary.md#supersession)
6	
7	## 1 · What this repo is
8	
9	A ledger with views. Records are filed by **what they are** (provenance
10	class), immutable and dated; **what they're about** is computed as
11	derived views (tags → indexes, deps → threads). What-is-known is always
12	derivable from what happened — never the reverse.
13	
14	## 2 · Content classes — there are exactly three
15	
16	- **`exchanges/`** — the ledger. Immutable, dated, flat records of
17	  one-shot operator↔agent interactions. The only place agent content is
18	  born. Named `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`; schema in
19	  [exchange-schema.md](exchange-schema.md).
20	- **`docs/`** — the governing layer: doctrine, policy, purpose, intent,
21	  invariants, contracts, methods, tripwires. Defined by **ratification,
22	  not species of author**: operator-authored, or agent-originated and
23	  promoted by the operator. Authorship is carried by markers; an
24	  agent-originated doc carries a provenance link to its birth exchange.
25	- **`tools/`** — deterministic executable machinery. The directory marks
26	  role (plumbing); markers and provenance still mark authorship.
27	
28	External sources enter as **footnotes** in the doc that cites them —
29	inclusion is always explicit, never general. Where preservation or depth
30	matters, the act of capturing the source is itself an exchange, and the
31	footnote also points at that record (link-rot mitigation).
32	
33	## 3 · Vocabulary and views
34	
35	- **`taxonomy/`** — the tag vocabulary as a directory tree. Vocabulary
36	  only, never content. Each leaf holds an `index.md` (a `#derived` view
37	  listing every record tagged with that path — links only, no copies;
38	  the leaf index is also what lets git track the tree). New tags may be
39	  proposed by the classifier; they exist once the operator commits them.
40	- **`threads/`** — `#derived` views materializing the deps graph: chains
41	  of exchanges by lineage. Regenerated by `tools/derive_threads.exs`.
42	
43	Views answer "what else is about this" (indexes) and "what did this grow
44	out of" (threads). Both are projections of the ledger — regenerate, never
45	hand-edit.
46	
47	## 4 · The nursery rule
48	
49	All agent content is born in the ledger, as an exchange. Promotion out of
50	the ledger is the operator's ratifying act, and there are exactly two
51	promotion targets: **docs** (it governs) and **tools** (it runs).
52	Everything else stays in the ledger and is referenced by path.
53	
54	## 5 · Authorship markers — every markdown file carries exactly one
55	
56	- `#human-authored` — the operator wrote it.
57	- `#agent-authored` — a model wrote it; the file carries a provenance
58	  link to the exchange that produced it.
59	- `#derived` — a deterministic tool emitted it; regenerate, never edit.
60	
61	Exchange files are composite: their sections carry the markers
62	(`## Prompt` `#human-authored`, `## Response` `#agent-authored`,
63	`## Side Effects` `#derived`).
64	
65	## 6 · Mutability regimes — three, and only three
66	
67	- **Immutable**: everything under `exchanges/` (sidecars included). The
68	  window closes at commit; before the commit, correcting a proposed field
69	  by hand is the audit working, not a violation.
70	- **Edit-in-place with dated supersession**: docs. Invariants in
71	  particular are append-and-supersede — superseded entries stay, dated;
72	  silent edits are forbidden.
73	- **Regenerated**: `#derived` views. Overwritten wholesale by their tool.
74	
75	## 7 · Sidecars — evidence is kept, never deleted
76	
77	Every capture persists the harness's raw JSON stream — including any
78	tool-use and tool-result records — as
79	`exchanges/envelopes/<same-basename>.json`, together with the shown-list
80	(what evidence the classifier was given). Verdicts about evidence never
81	destroy the evidence: a verdict without its evidence is unfalsifiable.
82	Any future retention policy is operator-ratified and executed by a
83	deterministic script — never an agent turn.
84	
85	## 8 · Ratification and commits
86	
87	No agent ever commits. Every commit is operator-made and gated by the
88	checks (`tools/check_all.exs`, wired via `tools/hooks/pre-commit`). The
89	operator's commit is the ratification event for everything in it —
90	including machine-proposed metadata the operator has read and accepted.
91	
92	## 9 · No silent caps
93	
94	Whenever machinery bounds coverage — a top-k, a truncation, a sample —
95	the bound is recorded where the result lands (sidecar or Side Effects).
96	"Found nothing" is meaningless unless what was searched is on record.
97	
98	## 10 · Prerequisites
99	
100	git · Elixir 1.14+ (1.18+ recommended) · jq 1.6+ (the tools' JSON
101	engine) · the `claude` CLI as inference backend #1
102	([backend-contract.md](backend-contract.md)). Elixir presence is a
103	declared repo prerequisite: agent and CI environments provision it; the
104	pre-commit shim fails loudly if it is missing rather than degrading.

I've already gathered the relevant facts below. Do NOT search the filesystem — just reason over what's given and write the evaluation. Two things are being asked:

(1) Evaluate the ACCURACY of a new #human-authored paragraph the user (the operator) just added to docs/workflow.md, section "## The unit of work is the cycle", sitting directly above the pre-existing #agent-authored paragraph in the same section.

(2) Evaluate the IDEA of maintaining "duplicate stated docs" this way — i.e., a human paraphrase and an agent-authored formal paragraph coexisting permanently in the same section, both describing the same concept.

+#human-authored
+The idea behind the workflow in this system is similar to that of a feature branch - the user creates a branch `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, where <name> is the expected focus of a series of exchanges.  A cycle is a branch: `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, named when it is opened
 — intent declared before the work exists. A cycle carries any change
 class — exchanges and sidecars, docs, tools, taxonomy nodes — with one

 `main` and are written only by the derivation job.

- "## exchange" — "The atomic record class: one operator↔agent interaction — prompt verbatim, response verbatim, derived Side Effects — filed flat, dated, immutable in exchanges/, named before the answer exists."

- Duplicate docs: assess whether having both a human paraphrase and an agent-authored formal paragraph permanently coexist in one section is sound, given the repo's own stated mutability regime for docs/ (edit-in-place WITH dated supersession, not indefinite duplication) and the constitution's "single source of truth flows one direction" principle.
